chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who applies kohl (in the eyes) with a needle from an intoxicant, Allah Mighty and Majestic will apply (in his eyes) a needle from Fire.

key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (an honorific title for Allah)
key_terms.كَحَلَهُ: He applied kohl (verb form indicating the action done to the subject)
key_terms.مِيلٍ: A needle or small stick used for applying kohl to the eyes

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using wine or intoxicants for medical treatment in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'dissimulation' (takhrij al-khamr) where the intoxicating property of wine remains potent even when used externally as kohl, thereby incurring spiritual punishment. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the essence of the intoxicant is not nullified by its change in form or application, serving as a warning against seeking medicinal exemptions for prohibited substances.
